{"slug": "kodely-vs-wordpress", "title": "Kodely vs WordPress: Which Site Builder Should You Use? (2026)", "metaTitle": "Kodely vs WordPress: Which Should You Use? (2026)", "metaDescription": "Kodely vs self-hosted WordPress compared on pricing, code ownership, hosting, plugins, maintenance, and security so you can pick the right one.", "targetKeyword": "kodely vs wordpress", "category": "Comparisons", "bodyHtml": "

WordPress and Kodely solve overlapping problems in opposite ways. WordPress (the free, self-hosted software from WordPress.org, not the separate WordPress.com hosted subscription) gives you a mature open-source CMS, full file access, and a plugin ecosystem that covers almost anything you can imagine. Kodely gives you a chat interface that writes a real React app for you and publishes it in one click, with none of the server management. Here is the honest comparison, including where each one actually wins.

TL;DR verdict

CategoryKodelyWordPress (self-hosted)
How you buildDescribe it in chat; AI generates real codeThemes, page builders, and plugins
Code ownershipView and copy source in-app; no export yetFull file access from day one
HostingFree *.kodely.site subdomain, one clickYou buy and manage hosting yourself
Cost modelFree 750 credits, then pay-as-you-go top-upsSoftware is free; hosting and premium plugins cost extra
MaintenanceNone — no server, no updates to runOngoing: core, theme, and plugin updates
Ecosystem depthFrontend only, growingHuge — WooCommerce, forms, SEO, membership, booking
Security burdenHandled by Kodely; secrets scanned before publishOn you; plugins are a common attack vector

Pricing and the credit model

WordPress itself is free and open source. What costs money is everything around it: hosting, a domain, and often premium plugins or themes for anything beyond a basic blog. WordPress.com is a separate, hosted product with its own subscription tiers — if someone says WordPress is a monthly fee, they are usually thinking of that, not the self-hosted software.

Kodely works differently: it is metered by AI usage, not a subscription. Every new account gets 750 credits free, no credit card required. If you need more, top-ups are $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits (most popular), or $90 for 6,000 credits, and credits never expire. If a generation fails to compile, you are not charged for it. There is no separate hosting bill on top — publishing to your *.kodely.site URL is included.

Do you own the code

This is WordPress's clearest structural advantage. Self-hosted WordPress gives you direct file access to your themes, plugins, and database from the moment you install it. You can move hosts, fork a plugin, or edit PHP directly whenever you want.

Kodely generates a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application — genuine component files, not a locked-in page-builder format — and you can view and copy that source from inside the app. What Kodely does not have yet is a code export or zip download, so you cannot currently pull the full project out to run on your own infrastructure. If self-hosting or full portability is a requirement today, WordPress wins outright.

Hosting and going live

With WordPress, going live means choosing a host, configuring DNS, installing SSL, and keeping the server patched — or paying someone to do it. It is flexible, including custom domains from the start, but it is a real setup step.

With Kodely, publishing is one click. Your site goes live on a real public URL at <name>.kodely.site, free, with no separate hosting account to configure. The tradeoff is that Kodely does not support custom domains yet — you are on the kodely.site subdomain for now, which matters if branded domain hosting is non-negotiable for your launch.

Backend and plugin depth

WordPress's plugin library is its strongest asset for anything beyond a marketing page: WooCommerce for e-commerce, Gravity Forms or similar for lead capture, Yoast or Rank Math for SEO, MemberPress for gated content, and booking plugins for appointments. If your site needs a database-backed feature, there is very likely a plugin for it already.

Kodely currently generates frontend applications only — it does not generate backend logic, databases, authentication, or payment processing. If you need an e-commerce checkout, a login system, or a booking database today, WordPress with the right plugins is the more capable choice.

Maintenance burden

This is where Kodely's design pays off. A self-hosted WordPress site is not a one-time build — it is ongoing work. Core updates, theme updates, and plugin updates all need to happen regularly, and plugin conflicts after an update are a routine headache. Someone has to own that, indefinitely.

Kodely has no server to patch and no plugin stack to keep in sync, because there is no server or plugin stack exposed to you at all. Changes happen by describing them in chat, and every successful generation is a checkpoint, so rolling back a change you do not like is free and instant. There is nothing to maintain between edits.

Security

WordPress's popularity is also its biggest security liability: because so many sites run it, and because third-party plugins vary wildly in code quality, WordPress sites are one of the most common targets for automated hacking attempts, almost always through vulnerable or outdated plugins. Keeping a WordPress site secure means staying current on updates and vetting every plugin you install.

Kodely removes that entire attack surface for you — there is no plugin marketplace to introduce third-party vulnerabilities, and every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live.

Best for

Choose WordPress if you need e-commerce, a membership system, complex custom functionality, a custom domain immediately, or full ownership and portability of your files, and you are willing to own ongoing maintenance (or pay a host that does it for you).

Choose Kodely if you want a real coded site live in minutes with zero server or plugin maintenance, you are building a marketing site, landing page, portfolio, or frontend-only product, and you are comfortable on a kodely.site subdomain for now while the platform adds custom domains and export.

FAQ

Is Kodely built on WordPress?

No. Kodely generates an independent Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS application from scratch for each project. It has no relationship to WordPress's codebase or plugin system.

Can I move a Kodely site to WordPress later?

Not directly today. Kodely does not yet offer a code export or zip download, only in-app viewing and copying of the generated source files, so migrating the raw project elsewhere is not currently supported.

Does Kodely support WooCommerce-style e-commerce?

Not yet. Kodely does not generate backend logic, databases, or payment processing, so an online store with checkout is currently better suited to WordPress with WooCommerce.

Is self-hosted WordPress really free?

The WordPress.org software itself is free and open source. You still pay for hosting, a domain, and usually some premium plugins or themes, which is different from a WordPress.com hosted subscription plan.

Do I need to know how to code to use Kodely?

No. You describe what you want in plain English in the chat interface, and Kodely writes and edits the actual component code for you.

Ready to see it for yourself? Start building free on Kodely and get 750 credits with no credit card required.
